gloss: no; whether or not; nay, rather

definitions.gloss: whether or not, yes or no
definitions.explanation: Used to present an alternative or question about whether something is so or not. Often appears in compound expressions.
Used to correct or upgrade a previous statement, similar to 'nay' or 'or rather' in English. Literary.

examples.english: Opinions were divided between for and against.

examples.japanese: {参加|さんか}するか{否|いな}かは{本人|ほんにん}の{自由|じゆう}だ。
examples.english: Whether or not to participate is up to the individual.

examples.japanese: この{提案|ていあん}を{受|う}け{入|い}れるか{否|いな}かは、{今後|こんご}の{会議|かいぎ}で{決定|けってい}される。
examples.english: Whether or not to accept this proposal will be decided at a future meeting.

examples.japanese: {数十人|すうじゅうにん}、{否|いな}、{数百人|すうひゃくにん}が{集|あつ}まった。
{難|むずか}しい、{否|いな}、ほぼ{不可能|ふかのう}だと{言|い}えるだろう。
examples.english: It could be called difficult — or rather, nearly impossible.

examples.japanese: それは{優|すぐ}れた{作品|さくひん}だった。{否|いな}、{傑作|けっさく}と{呼|よ}ぶべきものだった。
examples.english: It was an excellent work. Nay, it was what should be called a masterpiece.

notes:
USAGE:
Sense 1 commonly appears in the pattern ～か{否|いな}か (whether or not ~), which is formal and used in written Japanese. In compounds like {賛否|さんぴ} (pros and cons) and {安否|あんぴ} (safety/well-being), {否|ひ} is read with its on'yomi. Sense 2 is literary and rhetorical, used to correct or strengthen a previous statement.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ～か{否|いな}か: whether or not ~
- {否|いな}、～: nay, rather ~

COMPOUNDS:
- {賛否|さんぴ}: pros and cons, for and against
- {安否|あんぴ}: safety, well-being
- {可否|かひ}: propriety, approval or rejection
- {否定|ひてい}: denial, negation

SIMILAR WORDS:
{否|いな} is literary. The casual equivalent for "no" is いいえ or いや. The related entry {否|いや} (no, reluctance) has a different nuance, expressing dislike or refusal.
